qa_pairs.question:
Answer ONLY from the uploaded sources. Ignore any prior conversation entirely.
Verdict per claim: CONFIRMED / PARTIAL / NOT IN SOURCES. Quote the sentence for CONFIRMED or PARTIAL.
Do NOT infer or use general knowledge.

1. Users of manual expense trackers request AI-assisted entry, such as receipt or screenshot import, or natural-language parsing, AT ALL (regardless of ranking).
2. That request is the SINGLE MOST COMMON or TOP request from manual-tracker users.
3. Users of manual trackers request sovereign sync via iCloud or Dropbox.
4. Users request lifetime or one-time pricing, e.g. Buckets at $64 and Zeroed at $39.99.
5. Users request CSV or Mint importers / migration tools.
6. On-device or local processing of receipts is specifically valued for privacy reasons.
qa_pairs.answer:
1. **CONFIRMED**: Users of manual expense trackers discuss the use of AI to reduce the friction of manual entry and find it a sensible solution for tailoring tools to their needs.
> "Honestly this is the sort of project where getting an AI to do it makes sense. I ended up getting Claude on it, gave it a sample of what a CSV extract from my bank... and within about 1h I had a working self hosted totally local finance app tailored to my needs." [1]

2. **NOT IN SOURCES**: The sources do not identify AI-assisted entry as the "single most common" request; in fact, one provider of manual-first software identifies automatic bank sync as their most frequent request.
> "The most common request we get is, 'When will you add Plaid for automatic bank sync?' Our answer is always the same: we won't." [2]

3. **CONFIRMED**: Users who prioritize privacy and local control explicitly request models where they control the machine and sync mechanism to avoid third-party data storage.
> "I would prefer a different model where open source code run on a machine I control is the only place my banking credentials are used... And ideally these apps would have no Internet access so they could not store any of said data on remote servers." [3]

4. **CONFIRMED**: Users express "subscription fatigue" regarding annual fees and report dissatisfaction when companies discontinue one-time or "lifetime" purchase options.
> "Users are dissatisfied with the lack of a fully functional free version, increased subscription prices and discontinuation of the lifetime purchase option." [4]

5. **CONFIRMED**: Following the closure of major services like Mint, users actively seek migration tools and value the ability to import data via CSV to maintain their financial history.
> "The other plus about Piere is that it allowed me to import years of Mint data, though the end result wasn’t ideal." [5]
> "Are you using bank sync or do you import via CSV?... I don't see an easy way to import my transactions via CSV because my bank is weird..." [6]

6. **CONFIRMED**: On-device processing of sensitive financial information, such as receipt OCR or screenshot parsing, is specifically highlighted as a privacy feature that ensures data does not leave the user's device.
> "Every transaction you enter, every receipt you scan with the on-device OCR, every chart generated lives on your phone or computer. It never touches our servers." [7]
> "Finny’s local OCR engine parses these images in batches, extracting transaction details locally without transferring bank login credentials to external servers." [8]
